# A quartic endpoint at which polyconvex extraction has no budget

This is a construction/reduction, not a quasiconvexity counterexample.
The final ordinary-heat question in Section 6 remains OPEN. The separate
`POLYNOMIAL_BARRIER.md` resolves it negatively only for polynomial
primitives, and more generally for 2-form coefficients C² at the origin.

All matrices and coefficients below are real. Set

    A=[[a,b],[c,d]], T=a²+b²+c²+d², q=ad−bc,
    x=a²+c²−b²−d²,
    F*(A)=T²+12q²+4qx.                                      (1)

The cone in Sections 1–3 consists of ALL 35-dimensional homogeneous
quartic POLYNOMIALS on R²ˣ². Summands have no imposed objectivity,
even-Hopf structure, or symmetry. A polyconvex summand can use an
arbitrary convex representative on the minors; its lift need not be
polynomial. Nonpolynomial homogeneous summands are not covered.

## 1. Rank-one convexity and positivity

Write y=2(ab+cd), z=2q. Then T²=x²+y²+z² and

    F*=x²+y²+2xz+4z².

The quadratic form on (x,y,z) is positive definite, so F*>0 off zero.
For quartics, D²F(A)[R,R]=D²F(R)[A,A]. Therefore it suffices to check
the whole Hessian at rank-one R. The literal acoustic calculation in
sol9/hopf/PROOF.md §1, specialized to beta=1,r=4, gives after positive
Schur elimination

    N=[[1−s,−2 sin(theta)], [−2 sin(theta),7−3s]],
    s=cos²(theta), det N=3(1−s)², 0≤s≤1.

N is positive semidefinite, including s=1. This proves ROC everywhere.
No strict ROC margin is asserted. The accepted sol9 calculation is an
input; the exact endpoint/face work below is new to this packet.

## 2. Two acoustic zero orbits expose a two-dimensional face

For an arbitrary quartic G, let

    f_G(A,eta,xi)=D²G(A)[eta⊗xi,eta⊗xi].

Let R_theta=[[C,−D],[D,C]], without requiring C²+D²=1; homogeneity
pays arbitrary C,D. Direct substitution into (1) gives f_F*=0 at

    A=[[-D,C],[C,D]], eta=(C,D), xi=(1,0);            (orbit 1)
    A=[[C,−D],[D,C]], eta=(C,D), xi=(0,1).            (orbit 2)

Suppose F*=G+H with G,H ROC quartics. Then f_G,f_H≥0 and both vanish
on both displayed orbits. Every first derivative of each nonnegative
polynomial with respect to the eight variables (A,eta,xi) vanishes
there. Expand the eight derivative identities for each orbit in C,D.
They are linear constraints on the 35 coefficients of G.

# Exact polynomial/regularity barrier, without an SOS assumption

Use F* and C(A)[h] from `THEOREM_REDUCTION.md`. The theorem here is:

**There is no closed 2-form Omega with coefficients C² near the
origin such that (5) is nonnegative for every A,h. In particular no
polynomial 1-form of ANY degree supplies such a completion. The same
holds for every constant mean-converging second-order flow.**

This excludes origin-regular closed-form heat proofs, not actual heat
monotonicity by all possible arguments. It does not exclude the full
angular exact-form class (Omega C¹ at zero), and does not prove non-QC.

## 1. Why homogeneous quadratic coefficients suffice for this theorem

Let W(Omega) denote the symmetric 6×6 matrix representing
Omega(B1,B2) on compatible h. Its acoustic symbol vanishes. If
W(Omega)≥0, every rank-one h=eta⊗xi⊗xi belongs to its kernel.
Those h span R²⊗Sym²(R²), which is the whole six-dimensional compatible
Hessian space. Hence W(Omega)=0. The map Omega→W(Omega) is injective:
the six wedge entries have respectively the unique monomials

    h0 h2, h0 h4, h0 h5, −h2 h3, h1 h5, h3 h5.

Thus a pure wedge term cannot be nonnegative unless Omega=0.

For a C² coefficient field, Taylor-expand at zero. Positivity at A=0
forces Omega(0)=0 by this observation. Substituting A=tA0, dividing
by t and passing t↓0 forces the linear coefficient to vanish as well.
Divide the remaining inequality by t²: its limit is

    C_F*(A0)+W(Omega2(A0))≥0,                            (9)

where Omega2 is the quadratic Taylor coefficient. Closedness implies
d Omega2=0. Therefore existence of the original smooth completion
would imply a closed quadratic-coefficient completion. This argument
allows a nonhomogeneous field, not just polynomial primitives.

If alpha is C³, d alpha is C²; any polynomial alpha is therefore
included. An angular homogeneous alpha=P5/T is not included merely
because its coefficients happen to be C² at zero.

# A strict open obstruction to polynomial/regular heat decompositions

The degenerate endpoint obstruction persists for strictly rank-one-convex
quartics, even when a finite decomposition uses arbitrarily many different
constant mean-converging flows. The proof does not assert global closure
or convexity of the union of those flow classes. Instead it constructs a
closed outer class, proves that the endpoint is outside it, and uses the
pointed ROC cone to control all finite sums.

The conclusion is qualitative in its neighborhood radius. No numerical
epsilon0 or separating functional has been acquired. The full angular /
rational exact-form class remains OPEN and is not excluded.

convex minor representatives are allowed for P. All integrand summands
